rubric.result: I judged the eight task commits and the two merge-resolution edits. I left the content of #547/#558/#561/#562/#563 out, as instructed. T1: ToolRunner.run goes through processes.runAndWait and #spawned through processes.launch. The group kill goes through this.signal. SystemProcesses implements both methods with execFile/spawn, and ct-api gives one CtApi.#PROCESSES to every ToolRunner. T2: process.kill, the /bin/ps read and node-pty all live in SystemProcesses now. CheckedRunDelivery.#alive is an instance method over this.signal(pid, 0) and keeps the EPERM rule. PtyLiveSessions takes spawn, signal and inspectProcessTable as ProcessTable members with no default, and ct-api passes all three. T3: a grep of backend/src finds node:child_process, node-pty and process.kill only in process-border.ts. The worker's main builds SystemProcesses and still opens with the release. T4: ScriptedConversation answers by binary+argv+cwd, whatever the order, and raises UnscriptedRequest. T5: ProcessRatchet with LISTED. T6: the ledger and LedgerRows. T7: the instrument. T8: the baseline and the paragraph. One low gap in T6, below.

All eight TDD tests are in the diff and assert what the plan wrote. T1 'a_call_through_a_process_port_is_a_site_of_its_own' asserts sitesIn("this.processes.launch('git', [])\n",'x.ts') calls == ['launch']. T2 'the_process_table_read_carries_the_inspection_bounds' asserts that the double received INSPECTION_TIMEOUT_MS and INSPECTION_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES. T3 'the_border_is_the_only_module_of_src_that_imports_a_spawning_library' asserts Backend.importers(), a one-line wrapper over SpawnedChildren.importersUnder(Backend.ROOT), equals [join('infrastructure','process-border.ts')]. T4 includes the boundary: the same argv in /private/tmp raises. T5: unlisted and stale over temporary trees. T6: the broken row, then a row with ' > ' that passes. T7: 1/2 against 2/2 is a drop, and the same tally is not. T8: lines.covered of ct-api.ts > 0.

process-runner.ts states RunAndWaitOptions, RunFailure, RunOutcome, LaunchOptions and ProcessRunner with the plan's names, fields and parameter order. LaunchedProcess is structural. process-table.ts states TerminalOptions, TableRead, ProcessTable and TerminalSpawn = ProcessTable['openTerminal']. The only difference is added readonly modifiers on TerminalOptions, which change nothing. Terminal moved byte for byte, and no importer still reads it from pty-live-sessions.ts. The pty call site matches the Call site block. The CheckedRunDelivery Current state became an instance method over signal, and the optional alive port is gone. Task 3's Current states are applied. The prose contracts hold too: ScriptedConversation/Capture/UnscriptedRequest with its message, ProcessRatchet's four constants and three statics with both messages, and CoverageBaseline's REPORT/BASELINE/EXCLUDED rows with their from values, BaselineExists and the write/compare verbs. The package.json scripts and c8 ^11.0.0 are verbatim. Both Final texts, the ledger and the this-repository.md paragraph after line 300, are in the diff verbatim.

Every row the diff bears on holds its closed value. D-3: out of scope for slice 1. D-4: c8 over vitest run with the children counted, per-file lines and branches. D-5: no CI job added. D-6: one border, excluded in EXCLUDED together with ct-api's 'await CtApi.run(' and the worker's '  static async main('. D-7 and the rows for the ports and where they sit: both are base classes in infrastructure/ whose methods throw 'must implement'. D-8: captures under __tests__/captures/git/, headed with command, version and date. D-11: the ratchet lands with its list. D-13: only backend/conventions/this-repository.md is amended. D-14: the timeouts are untouched. The border: SystemProcesses extends ProcessRunner implements ProcessTable. Injection: ToolRunner takes processes and signal, CheckedRunDelivery takes signal, and PtyLiveSessions/HeadlessCallWorker/ClaudeCalls keep their field names and take the member types. The ledger path and headings hold. ProcessRatchet.LISTED is where the list lives. No flag.

Exemplars: process-runner.ts and process-table.ts use the port shape of tool-sessions.ts ('${this.constructor.name} must implement ...'). ScriptedConversation raises 'nobody wrote an answer for ...', like GitDouble. ProcessRatchet uses the census shape of spawned-children: a table, a tree walk, and the guard proven over temporary trees, as typescript-only.test.ts does. The ACCOUNTED rows carry the reasons the plan wrote. Rules I read: plugin/conventions/testing.md. Its sentence 'A double of a whole conversation answers by what it is asked, not by order, and raises when nobody wrote an answer' is met by ScriptedConversation.#matches and UnscriptedRequest. Its sentence 'the shape it declares comes from a real capture... the test names where its capture came from' is met by the capture headers. No new test file launches a process without the marker. style.md: no comments. coverage-baseline.ts runs its main behind an import.meta guard, the same way ct-api.ts boots. backend/conventions/this-repository.md: the paragraph is placed where the plan said, and the 'real processes by design' sentence is untouched. architecture.md/boundaries.md: dependencies arrive injected. SystemProcesses is built only in the composition roots (ct-api, the worker's main) and in test arrangements. defects.md, rule by rule. Closed vocabulary: Dimension is a union. CoverageBaseline.main compares argv against 'write' and 'compare' by hand, but that is a CLI boundary and an unknown verb throws rather than falling into a silent default, so this is not the defect. Raw map as the return value of logic: measured() returns Record<string, FileCoverage>. That is an index keyed by file path with typed values, not a record standing in for a struct by key lookup, and dropsAgainst treats an absent key as a named drop on purpose, as the plan asks. I judged it not a finding. Two fields that must agree: none added. RunOutcome's failure is null or a value by contract. Exclusion.from null for 'the whole file' is the plan's closed shape, not an invented sentinel. Errors named for what happens: UnscriptedRequest and BaselineExists are named for what happens. The repo declares no skills to load.

In this slice's own test files, the '-' lines only retype things: typeof spawn becomes ProcessRunner['launch'], and (signal) => ... becomes (read: TableRead) => .... Construction also changes: ToolRunner calls add processes and signal, and the PtyLiveSessions arranges that used the removed default now pass border.readTable. Every exec.calls assertion on the /bin/ps argv, options and bounds survives. I found no removed or relaxed expect( in the slice's test files. The removed assertions in api-server, start-plan, git-workspace, restart-recovery and similar files come from the #562/#563 merge, which is not this slice's work. The two resolution edits only add ports: signal on the recorded-pull-request test, and processes/signal next to #563's env in run-driver-mother.

Production code does the promised work. ToolRunner, SystemProcesses, CheckedRunDelivery.#alive, PtyLiveSessions.inspectProcessTable, HeadlessCallWorker and ClaudeCalls carry the routing through the ports. The scripted conversation, the ratchet, the ledger reader and the coverage instrument live under __tests__, which is where the plan puts them. Their tests exercise the real ToolRunner or the real census and walk rather than a hard-coded answer. The committed-baseline tests read the file that c8 wrote.

Every path this slice owns falls under a task's Files line. The captures, coverage, scripted-conversation and ratchet files each belong to one task. The many test files retyped for the ports fall under 'every test or fixture that builds a ToolRunner' (T1), 'the tests that build these classes' (T2) and 'the tests that build ClaudeCalls or HeadlessCallWorker' (T3). No declared path is left untouched. Out of scope holds: the frontend/, API.md and README changes all come from the merge. The vitest timeouts and the 'real processes by design' sentence are untouched, and no CI job is added. The plan amendment in task 5 replaces '-ge 17' with '-ge $(find ... -name '*-real-process.test.ts' | wc -l)'. That is justified: the merge of #563 left 15 marked files. The new command still demands that every marked file is listed, so it pins the same property and does not weaken the control.

I judged the new tests in spawned-children, pty-live-sessions, scripted-conversation, process-ratchet, ledger and coverage-baseline against the three blocking properties. Deterministic: no clock, network or randomness in any assertion. /private/tmp is only a cwd string, and the captures are fixed files. Isolated: every temporary tree comes from mkdtemp and is removed in finally, and no shared mutable state is asserted. Verifies real behaviour: each test asserts what ToolRunner, SpawnedChildren, ProcessRatchet, LedgerRows, CoverageBaseline or PtyLiveSessions produce, and each would go red with its production lines reverted. I report nothing beyond the three properties, so I did not load control-tower-loop:ct-test-driven-development.

findings.what: The CASE pattern of LedgerRows accepts any '`x > y`' cell, so a row whose case names no .test.ts file passes the format check, for example '| `foo > bar` | deleted without substitute — decided |'. The brief fixes the row shape as '<path>.test.ts > <name>', and the objective promises that a test names every row that breaks the format. The ledger is empty today, so nothing is affected yet.
